errors.text_span: both visualized as radial bar charts
errors.evidence: The charts are pie/donut charts (circular segmented charts), not radial bar charts.

errors.text_span: The "AttentionInfluence" chart shows a total of 12 primary categories
errors.evidence: The AttentionInfluence chart has more than 12 categories when counting all labeled segments. Looking at the chart, there are outer segments like Policy 1, Manage 2, Emerging tech 4, Materials 3, Infor tech 5, Events & people 6, Society & culture 10, Historical review 7, Materials 2, and inner/primary ones like Teaching & resources 15, Science & technology education 10, Diseases 11, Nutrition 5, Medical 6, Animal & Plant 13, Science 15, Health & Medicine 22, Education 25, Tech & Engineer 12, Fin & Law 3. The description arbitrarily assigns 12 as 'primary' categories which is inaccurate.
In the AttentionInfluence chart, Materials is labeled as 3, but there is also a 'Materials 2' shown separately as a different segment. The description conflates these.

The description does not mention that the charts have a two-tier/nested ring structure (inner ring with major categories and outer ring with subcategories), which is a key structural feature of these charts.
The description does not note that the labels use numerical counts (not percentages), and no percentage labels are shown inside slices.
The description does not mention that there is a 'Fin & Law 3' segment visible in the AttentionInfluence chart.
The description does not mention the 'Healthy education 2' segment visible in the FineWeb-Edu Classifier chart.

errors.text_span: The "FineWeb-Edu Classifier" chart displays 10 primary categories
errors.evidence: Similar to the AttentionInfluence chart, the FineWeb-Edu Classifier also has a nested two-tier structure. The description's categorization of 10 'primary' vs smaller segments is an arbitrary and inaccurate structural characterization.
The description does not note whether the charts include a legend. In this case, no separate legend is present—all labels are directly annotated.

In the FineWeb-Edu Classifier chart, the label reads 'Tech & Engineer 8' but the description's label placement context may be confusing as it's labeled '...' and '8' in the figure. This is approximately correct but the label in the chart shows 'Tech & ... 8' suggesting truncation.
